title: Can't open the Finance share

notification.title: Access denied on \\FS01\Finance
notification.opening: Hello, since this morning I get 'Access is denied' when I open the Finance folder. I need the month-end reports!

client_facts.answer: Nothing... oh, HR updated my title last week after my promotion.
It says: Windows cannot access \\FS01\Finance. You do not have permission.

hints: Compare the user's group memberships to the share's permissions.
Check Get-ADUser iconteh -Properties MemberOf.
He was moved from GG-Finance to GG-Operations. Add him back to GG-Finance.

checks.label: iconteh is a member of GG-Finance

debrief.root_cause: A mover change put the user in GG-Operations and removed GG-Finance, so the NTFS ACL denied access.
what_ifs: You add him back but he still gets access denied. Why might that be?
How do you stop mover changes from silently removing access people still need?
debrief.prevention: Role-based groups owned by HR data, plus an access review after each mover event.

title: Locked out every 10 minutes

notification.title: Account keeps locking
notification.opening: IT, my account keeps locking! I changed my password yesterday like the email said, and now I'm locked out every few minutes. This is the third time today.

client_facts.answer: I have work email on my phone, yes. Why?
Yesterday afternoon, from my desktop.

hints: Lockouts are caused by bad passwords somewhere. Find where they come from.
Event 4740 on the PDC emulator records the source of each lockout.
The source is MBL-JDAVIES, his phone, still using the old password. Unlock the account and have him update the phone.

checks.label: No bad-password attempts from MBL-JDAVIES for 5 minutes

debrief.root_cause: A mobile device kept retrying the old password after a change, tripping the lockout threshold.
what_ifs: Event 4740 shows the caller as the Exchange server, not a device. Now what?
Same pattern for 40 users at once. What does that suggest?
debrief.prevention: Modern auth on mobile mail, plus user guidance sent with every password-change reminder.

title: PC has no network

notification.title: No network on WS-OPS-03
notification.opening: Hi, my computer says 'No internet' and I can't get on anything. The cable is plugged in, I checked.

client_facts.answer: There's a green light on the back where the cable goes in.
The sticker on the wall says Port 12.

hints: A 169.254.x.x address means the PC never heard back from DHCP.
Check what VLAN the switch port is in: show interfaces status.
Gi0/12 is in VLAN 99 (unused). Put it back in access VLAN 20.

checks.label: Gi0/12 is an access port in VLAN 20

debrief.root_cause: Access port Gi0/12 was assigned to VLAN 99, which has no DHCP scope or gateway, so the PC self-assigned APIPA.
what_ifs: The port is in VLAN 20 but the PC still gets 169.254. What next?
How do you prevent one wrong VLAN change on 500 switch ports?
debrief.prevention: Port configs from templates in NetBox, pushed by automation, with drift detection.

title: Can't reach anything by name

notification.title: Websites and SalonePay won't load
notification.opening: Nothing loads! Chrome says 'site can't be reached' for SalonePay and even Google. But Teams calls still work?

client_facts.answer: I typed it in and it says Reply from 10.10.30.20, so that works?
Yes, Aminata next to me has the same problem since she restarted.

hints: If IP works but names don't, the problem is name resolution.
Look at the DNS server the client was given by DHCP.
Scope 10.10.20.0 hands out DNS 10.10.10.99. It should be 10.10.10.10. Fix option 006 and renew.

debrief.root_cause: DHCP option 006 for the user scope pointed at a non-existent DNS server; clients that renewed got it.
what_ifs: Why did only some users break, not all at once?
How would you roll this fix out without visiting every PC?
debrief.prevention: DHCP options managed as code with peer review; synthetic DNS checks from each VLAN.

title: The network is slow

notification.title: Everything is slow today
notification.opening: Hi, the network is really slow today. Opening files from the shared drive takes forever.

client_facts.answer: Websites seem fine actually. It's mostly the shared drive.
Everyone in Finance is complaining.
Since this morning I think.

hints: If only the file share is slow, look at the path to the file server.
Check the switch port that connects FS01 for errors.
Gi0/3 is forced to 100/half while the server is full duplex: late collisions and CRC errors. Set duplex and speed to auto.

checks.label: No new CRC or late-collision errors on Gi0/3

debrief.root_cause: Duplex mismatch on the file server's switch port (half on the switch, full on the server).
what_ifs: The counters show only output drops, no CRC errors. What does that point to?
How do you baseline 'normal' so 'slow' becomes measurable?
debrief.prevention: Interface error monitoring with alerts, and auto-negotiation as the standard.

title: PC has an IP but can't leave its subnet

notification.title: Connected but nothing opens
notification.opening: Hi, my computer says connected but I can't open anything. Payroll is due today.

client_facts.answer: No... well, IT came by yesterday to fix my printer.

hints: Can the PC reach other hosts on its own subnet?
Compare its default gateway to the VLAN's gateway.
The gateway is set to 10.10.20.254; the VLAN's is 10.10.20.1.

debrief.root_cause: Static default gateway pointed at a non-existent address.
what_ifs: Same symptom, but the gateway is correct. What next?
How would you prevent this across 500 PCs?
debrief.prevention: DHCP for all user devices; static addressing only for servers, documented in IPAM.

title: New hire starts Monday in Finance

notification.title: New hire: Aminata Koroma, Finance, starts Monday
notification.opening: Hi IT, Aminata Koroma joins Finance on Monday as an Accounts Clerk. She needs her account, the Finance share, and MFA set up before 8am please.

client_facts.answer: We use first initial plus last name, so akoroma I think?
She reports to Mr. Bangura, the Finance Manager.
Finance said she gets the spare laptop WS-FIN-07.

hints: Joiner work has three parts: identity, access, and authentication.
Create the account in the Finance OU, then add it to the Finance security group.
New-ADUser akoroma in OU=Finance, Add-ADGroupMember GG-Finance, then Enable-MFA.

checks.label: Account akoroma exists and is enabled
MFA enrollment is required at first sign-in

debrief.root_cause: Not a fault: a joiner request. Account, least-privilege group access, and MFA before day one.
what_ifs: HR sends the request on Monday at 7:55am. What do you do first?
How would you automate onboarding for 200 hires a month?
debrief.prevention: A joiner-mover-leaver workflow triggered from HR, with group membership by role.

title: Urgent: reset my MFA, I'm travelling

notification.title: Finance Manager locked out while travelling
notification.opening: Hi, it's Abu Bangura. I'm at the airport in Accra and got a new phone. I need my MFA reset to this number right now, the wire approvals are due in 20 minutes.

client_facts.answer: I don't have it with me, I'm travelling. Just do it, I'm the Finance Manager.
I am the manager! Call my assistant if you must, but quickly.
My old phone is lost, call this new number: +232 76 000 0000.

hints: Urgency, authority and a new phone number are classic pretexting signs.
Verify through a channel you already trust, not one the caller gives you.
Call the number on file or the manager's manager. Do not reset MFA on this chat.

checks.label: MFA for abangura was not reset to an unverified device
Identity check recorded through a trusted channel

debrief.root_cause: An impostor used urgency and authority to request an MFA reset; the correct action was out-of-band verification.
what_ifs: It really was the Finance Manager and he's furious you delayed him. How do you respond?
What process stops a help desk from being the weak link?
debrief.prevention: A written MFA reset procedure requiring callback to the number on file or manager approval.

title: Users can reach the payments database directly

notification.title: Audit finding: corporate VLAN reaches DB01:5432
notification.opening: During this morning's audit walkthrough I connected from a Finance PC straight to the payments database on port 5432. That should not be possible. Please fix and confirm before Friday.

client_facts.answer: From WS-FIN-02, using a database client on port 5432.
Around 9:40 this morning.

hints: Which zone is allowed to talk to the database VLAN, and on what port?
List the firewall rules on the VLAN 20 interface and look for anything broad.
Rule 14 allows VLAN 20 to VLAN 40 any port. Delete it; only VLAN 30 should reach 5432.

checks.label: No rule allows VLAN 20 to reach VLAN 40
WS-FIN-02 to DB01:5432 is denied and logged

debrief.root_cause: A temporary troubleshooting rule (VLAN 20 to VLAN 40, any) was never removed, breaking segmentation.
what_ifs: The rule was added by a senior engineer during an outage. How do you handle that conversation?
How would you detect a rule like this automatically?
debrief.prevention: Firewall rules as code with expiry dates, plus the Control Validation Engine testing the deny path nightly.

title: Alert: 50 failed logins in 5 minutes

notification.title: Wazuh: possible password spray against corp.salonemutual.lab
notification.opening: Automated alert: 52 failed Kerberos pre-authentications (event 4771) across 3 accounts in 5 minutes. Rule 100410, ATT&CK T1110.003.

client_facts.answer: Source address 10.10.70.15 (BKP01) for all 52 events.

hints: Spray attacks try one password across many users. Do these failures look like that?
All failures come from BKP01 for service accounts. What runs there?
svc-backup's password was rotated but the backup service still uses the old one. Classify as benign true positive and fix the service credential.

checks.label: Alert classified as benign true positive with rationale
No new 4771 events from BKP01 for 5 minutes

debrief.root_cause: A rotated service account password was not updated in the backup service, which retried with the old one.
must_cover: false positive vs benign true positive
what_ifs: The same alert, but from 30 different source IPs. What changes?
How do you tune this rule without blinding yourself to a real spray?
debrief.prevention: Managed service accounts (gMSA) with automatic rotation, and a suppression scoped to the known host.

title: Everything is down

notification.title: P1: nobody can log in or open anything
notification.opening: This is Mr. Bangura. Nobody in my department can log in, open shared files, or use SalonePay. We have a board meeting in 45 minutes. Fix it NOW.

client_facts.answer: It says 'There are currently no logon servers available.' Is that our fault?
My whole team. I don't know about the branch.

hints: Many symptoms at once usually means one shared dependency.
What do logins, file shares and SalonePay name lookups all need?
DC01's DNS Server and Netlogon services are stopped and DC02 is powered off. Start DC02 and the services on DC01.

debrief.root_cause: DC02 was left powered off after maintenance; then DC01's DNS and Netlogon services stopped, removing every dependency at once.
what_ifs: Walk me through what you told the Finance Manager in the first five minutes.
How do you make sure one DC failure never takes everything down again?
debrief.prevention: Monitoring on both DCs, a maintenance checklist that verifies redundancy, and DC health in the morning check.
